fused_findings: Generation-1 clean_machine_acceptance.py is a preserved historical ABI, not the whole current WP1110 acceptance path. Exact-current successor lineage must be inspected before declaring a field absent from F2.

WP1110 G2 release_artifact_subject.py plus artifact_bound_clean_machine.py already implement exact unopened archive subject binding and clean-machine subject consistency at repository-component scope.

WP1110 G3 receipt_content_binding.py already binds exact external prehandoff receipt bytes; current WP1107 release_archive.py uses ZIP_STORED plus canonical metadata and exact whole-archive rebuild/equality, so zlib cross-host compressor variability is not a current V1 blocker.

Current handoff content identity is strong at repository-component scope, but cryptographic producer-origin authentication is not observed in the inspected path. This is a separate property, not a defect under every threat model.

SLSA/Sigstore style signature/root verification becomes relevant if F2 must defend against wholesale package+receipt replacement by an untrusted distributor or must prove independent producer identity.
TUF-class metadata becomes relevant only if F2 grows an actual update/repository channel where freshness/rollback/mix-and-match are product threats.
Do not delay the immediate WP1207/owner-host executable frontier for mandatory signing infrastructure without an explicit distribution-threat requirement.
